version: LightOnOCR-3-4B on LightOn's official demo page (no account)
genus: Turns photos of pages into text
feeds_on: A photo of a page, or a PDF
free_tier: Free demo, no account; model free to download
test: One photo of a handwritten note (licensed, Unsplash) on the official demo with its defaults; compared word by word with our own transcription written before the test.

conditions.value: A photo of a handwritten note, 46 words (free from Unsplash)
LightOn's free demo page, in a web browser
Left as they were (4B model, Grounding)

runs.output_text: Butch Left him with B Boaze, when I went home Nevada St, with Jimmy could only take the one cat. My own dearly loved Jimmy Butel was knocked down in Richmond St and killed He was a very pretty thing. Love

seconds_note: From clicking Run OCR to the result, rebuilt from screenshot file times (our script stopped on a later step; see raw/auto/run.json). Not re-run.
verdict_reason: Free, fast and 42 of 46 words right on hard handwriting, but three misreads change what the note says: the cat's name, who loved him, and the last line. For handwriting you would still have to check every line, so we'd skip it for that job.
lesson: OCR on handwriting is a first draft: always read it against the original, especially names and the last line.
use_for: A quick first draft you'll check

deductions: factual error: Mum read as 'My own' -10
factual error: 'Ginger Tom.' read as 'thing. Love' -10

score.notes: Work drawer. Quality 50 - 30 = 20. Speed: about 4 s, under 60 s = 15. Free plan: no login 5, no published limit 10, demo only 1 = 16. Price: not published = 3. 54 is between 45 and 60, so the catch decides: it changed the note's meaning, which matters most for handwriting, hence Released.
